title: UPDATE: ChatGPT's U.S. Paid Subscribers Triple Those of Claude and Gemini

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Fewer than 5% of adults in the United States pay for access to artificial intelligence assistants, as mass adoption has not yet translated into widespread subscription revenue. According to a new report from a16z, only 4.5% of U.S. consumers pay for services like ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude, but spending is concentrated among an elite group of power users. The top 1% of payers spend an average of $903 per month on personal credit cards, up from $504 in January 2025, and collectively drive more revenue than the bottom 50% of payers combined, whereas the median customer spends just $25.

OpenAI maintains a commanding lead with three times as many paid U.S. subscribers as Anthropic or Google. While ChatGPT's scale is dominant, including 1B+ monthly actives on mobile, Anthropic has gained traction by passing Gemini in U.S. paid subscriptions and leads in spending in Montana, California, and Massachusetts. The report also highlights a disconnect between usage and monetization, noting that 29 of the top 50 revenue-generating AI firms do not even appear on a16z's traffic lists for web or mobile visits.

selectedTweets.bestBit: ChatGPT still holds the throne, now with 1B+ monthly actives on mobile
selectedTweets.text:
The seventh edition of our Top 100 Consumer AI Apps is here.

New this time: a revenue leaderboard, alongside the usual web and mobile traffic rankings.

Three years ago we published the first edition. ChatGPT was #1, Claude was unranked, and the entire category was chatbots, image generators, and not much else.

In today's edition:

- ChatGPT still holds the throne, now with 1B+ monthly actives on mobile

- Claude has climbed to #3 on web with nearly 1B monthly visits

- The category has expanded to vibe coding (Lovable, Cursor, Replit), music (Suno), design (Figma), voice (ElevenLabs), video (Higgsfield, Kling), agents (Manus), and even hardware (Plaud)

Full breakdown from @omooretweets: https://t.co/J9edFBQvCN

selectedTweets.bestBit: Revenue data shows a 3x lead over both Claude and Gemini in U.S. paid subscribers
selectedTweets.text:
ChatGPT was the pioneer, and remains the clear leader.

Revenue data shows a 3x lead over both Claude and Gemini in U.S. paid subscribers - which is even more extreme globally.

Claude made real gains the past six months, crossing DeepSeek and Grok in traffic and Gemini in subs. https://t.co/4w2HQnUy0k

selectedTweets.bestBit: The top 1% spend $903 / month on AI on consumer cards alone
selectedTweets.text:
Fewer than 5% of Americans pay for AI - and even in this group, spend is HEAVILY concentrated.

The top 1% spend $903 / month on AI on consumer cards alone (work spend is even higher).

They drive more revenue than the entire bottom 50% of spenders combined. https://t.co/Ay9zxshQPv

selectedTweets.bestBit: ChatGPT already ranks in the top 20 global consumer products by number of paid subscribers
selectedTweets.text:
Despite that hurdle, ChatGPT already ranks in the top 20 global consumer products by number of paid subscribers.

The rest of the list is primarily media cos + a few retailers (Amazon, Costco).

As model COGS decline and products reach ad scale, we expect to see more free usage. https://t.co/DlZ2nSkL3y
